# Pesher Habakkuk Column 8 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 1QpHab (Cave 1), Col. 8 | **Condition:** Well preserved; contains famous Hab 2:3-4 passage

---

**8:1** "And as for what it says, 'so that the one who reads it may run' (Hab 2:2b) —

**8:2** its interpretation concerns the Teacher of Righteousness, to whom God

**8:3** made known all the mysteries of the words of His servants the prophets.

**8:4** 'For the vision is yet for an appointed time;

**8:5** it testifies of the end and does not lie' (Hab 2:3a).

**8:6** Its interpretation: the final age will be prolonged

**8:7** and will exceed all that the prophets said,

**8:8** for the mysteries of God are wonderful.

**8:9** 'If it tarries, wait for it; for it will surely

**8:10** come and will not delay' (Hab 2:3b).

**8:11** Its interpretation concerns the men of truth,

**8:12** the doers of the Torah, whose hands do not grow slack

**8:13** from the service of truth, even when the final age is prolonged for them.

**8:14** For all the appointed times of God will come in their due course,

**8:15** as He decreed for them in the mysteries of His prudence.

**8:16** 'Behold, the one whose soul is not upright within him — but the righteous one

**8:17** shall live by his faithfulness' (Hab 2:4). Its interpretation concerns all the observers of the Torah in the House of Judah, whom God will deliver from the house of judgment because of their suffering and their faithfulness to the Teacher of Righteousness.

---
*LOGOS notes: Column 8 covers Hab 2:2-4. This translation maintains formal equivalence while rendering readable English. The pesher (interpretation) sections apply Habakkuk's prophecy to the Qumran community's historical situation. Key figures: Teacher of Righteousness, Wicked Priest, Man of the Lie, the Kittim (Romans). "Interpretation" used consistently for pesher. Lacunae [...] indicate physical manuscript damage.*
